resources.string: So far %1$s ridden and %2$s %% battery used. The first estimate comes after about %3$s and %4$s %%.
Rides are recorded automatically. The first estimate comes after about %1$s and %2$s %% battery.
How far you can go right now is known once the bike is connected and reports its battery level.
≈ = little data in this level, estimated.
– = not ridden in this level yet.
Once the first rides are learned, the range of every level appears here.
How far you can still go
The ring shows %1$s in a straight line, i.e. there and back with the current battery.
Measured from where the bike was last parked.
The ring appears once the range has been learned.
The ring appears once the bike is connected and the battery level is known.
Without a current position the app cannot draw the ring.
Warns before the battery gets tight for the way home.
Way home %1$s, only %2$s left over, less than the reserve
Way home %1$s, the battery no longer covers it
Way home %1$s. Whether the battery covers it is known once the range is learned.
Way home %1$s. Whether the battery covers it is known once the bike is connected.
The way home is an estimate: straight line × %1$s for detours.
Set your home location and the app includes the way home.
No current position, so no answer about the way home right now.
No position on the road: allow location “all the time”, or open the app when you set off.
Without location access the app does not know where you are.
Location is switched off on the phone.
Tap the map to place your home.
Maximum range over the last six months
Season, temperature and riding style move this value as much as the battery itself.
A trend needs rides from at least two months, about %1$s per month.
Maximum range from %1$s to %2$s: from %3$s to %4$s
Only rides of %1$s or more count. Each counts with its battery level at rest before and after: the reading dips on climbs and comes back, so dips are not counted as used.
How far one percent goes is learned per battery level, as it need not be the same near full and near empty; where there are no rides yet, it continues the course of the measured ranges.
A way by road is about %1$s times the straight line; the ring and the way home use that.
How far each 10 % of battery takes you
The percentage on the display is not worth the same everywhere: it comes from the battery\'s voltage, which does not drop evenly. So the app learns for each 10 % band how far it goes.
Measured means: enough of your own rides in that band. Estimated bands continue the course of the measured ones: if the lower bands go less and less far, so do the ones below, but damped.
All bands together make up “Fully charged”; the safety margin is already taken off.
The bands appear once the app has learned your range from a few rides.
Not measured enough yet. Until then the app continues the course of the measured bands. It measures as soon as you ride in this range.
